verdict.rationale: Ultrametric's processes are the closest thing it has to automations, and it documents a few related capabilities of its own. Hosted process guides carry integer versions you can pin to a specific number (docs-11), `init --dry-run` previews skill-file changes before writing them (docs-8, verified in selfeval-2), and saved records keep history and revisions that guard against overwrites (docs-16, docs-17). These are versions of vendor-authored guides and run records, not user-defined automations, and committing skill files to git (docs-9) is a user-side workaround that earns no credit. Missing for 10: versioning of user-authored automations, a review/diff workflow for automation changes, any documented rollback or restore of records or runs, and hands-on verification of version history (hosted calls require login, per selfeval-4).
